morgan_customer: Hey team — seeing invalid JSON from structured mode when streaming. Our client JSON parser throws SyntaxError at the very first chunk. Repro steps below, intermittent but reproducible with long user inputs.

```bash
curl -s -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","mode":"structured","prompt":"summarize long notes","stream":true}'
```

Captured raw bytes from the TCP stream (truncated):
```json
{"record":{"id":123,"note":"Line1
Line2"}}
{"record":{"id":124,"note":"Another entry"}}
```
In the first chunk the string contains a literal newline (unescaped) between quotes which breaks standard JSON decoders. Request-id: r-0a9c3f. Can share pcap if helpful.

selena_support: Thanks Morgan. Can you confirm: model exactly \"redwood-1.1\"? Was this using any special flags (atomic_writes, structured_atomic, escape_non_printables)? Also, does non-streaming (/generate without stream) return valid JSON for the same prompt? :thinking:

morgan_customer: Confirm model=redwood-1.1. No special flags set from our side. Non-streaming returns fine (valid JSON). This only happens with stream=true and only sometimes. I attached a short pcap; I also noticed some payloads contain U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) literally in the payload, and one trace shows a surrogate split across two chunks (high surrogate at end of chunk A, low surrogate at start of chunk B) — client-side decoder chokes.

dave_eng-runtime: jumping in — thanks for the repro data. Quick hypothesis: we recently merged a serializer optimization that skips the full JSON-escaping pass for streaming frames to reduce CPU. It was meant to only run for plain-text paths but looks like structured/JSON mode still hit that path when payloads are short-lived. That would explain literal newlines / LS characters being emitted. Two separate problems to check: 1) unescaped non-printables (U+2028/U+2029/newlines) and 2) surrogate pair fragmentation across frame boundaries.

opsbot: Escalation created INC-2026 and assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026

dave_eng-runtime: For immediate mitigation you can set the per-request override: 
```json
{"stream":true, "structured_atomic_writes":true, "escape_non_printables":true}
```
This forces a safe serializer that performs full JSON escaping before emitting frames. Not ideal perf-wise but should avoid broken JSON. Can you try that and paste the response (raw) if it still fails?

morgan_customer: Tried the override — much better, fewer failures, but still saw one case where the stream ended mid-surrogate and produced invalid UTF-8 for our client decoder. Raw snippet (literal hex around boundary):
```
... 0xD8 0x3C [chunk boundary]
0xDC 0x5A ...
```
Which indicates a high surrogate (/D8 xx) at end of chunk, low surrogate starts next chunk. Our streaming parser assumes each chunk is a self-contained UTF-8 buffer which fails.

dave_eng-runtime: That's on us — streaming emitter needs to buffer until a full codepoint is available before flushing the frame. We're planning a small change: always ensure last N bytes do not end inside a UTF-8 multi-byte sequence (and for UTF-16 surrogate handling ensure we don't split the surrogate pair if the backend emits UCS2-like halves). I'll push a patch to staging: commit 0f3a9b2 with a guard in stream_flush().

opsbot: Deployment to staging for INT-rtm/serializer started (job #4871).

dave_eng-runtime: Patch deployed to staging. If you can re-run the same request-id or paste a new pcap I will validate. Also adding an additional end-to-end test that injects U+2028 and surrogate pairs into streaming outputs.

morgan_customer: Re-tested against staging after deploy — looks good, no JSON parse errors in a 2000-req stress run. Thanks! We rolled the mitigation flag off and production still looks stable. :tada:

selena_support: Closing the customer-facing escalation — sending Morgan the follow-up summary and the mitigation notes. Will monitor INC-2026 until the change lands in prod and add a regression test.

morgan_customer: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the fast turnaround.
